title: ICT and access

blocks.heading: ICT and access
blocks.text: ICT can support learning materials, communication and flexible access, but requires usable devices, power, connectivity, skills and suitable content. It may widen opportunities or deepen a digital gap. Learning gains need evidence; distributing devices alone does not establish teaching or access.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Apply the distinction
blocks.text: Explain the learning-access mechanism where an invented remote school receives devices but has no reliable power or teacher preparation for the material. Devices alone are not usable provision: power interrupts access and teachers lack the support to integrate the resources. Capacity to teach and use the material is needed before learning gains are established.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect the ideas
blocks.text: Connect to Health (7.2), modern roles (6.2) and Development (1.1). Separate access, participation and learning outcomes; do not assume a system label or device purchase establishes quality.
